title: Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution, Part II: the effective class number problem
summary: Extend the analytic class-number interfaces to Goldfeld’s effective lower bounds for imaginary quadratic fields. The proof combines positive Mellin kernels, modular elliptic L-functions with a third-order central zero, Gross–Zagier heights, genus theory and certified numerical estimates. Construct explicit discriminant bounds and a complete certified enumeration of the class number three fields, with independent arithmetic and analytic rank certificates for the two elliptic curves.
readme: The reader document is research/blueprint/readmes/AnalyticNumberTheoryPartII.md. Six layers lead from native class groups and existing modularity/height interfaces to the effective logarithmic lower bound and the complete class-number-three list. Sources are cited by theorem, section and printed page. Generic quadratic arithmetic, modularity, Gross–Zagier theory and validated numerics remain with their existing owners.

stages.title: Quadratic class numbers and ramified weights
stages.description: Import the existing ideal class number, fundamental discriminants, genus divisibility, and positive-definite binary-form reduction. Define the discriminant weight θ(d) excluding the largest prime. Prove p^h≥d/4 for a split prime and quantify agreement of the quadratic character with Liouville below this threshold. The form/class-group bijection, partial-zeta formulas and integrated nonaxial counting estimate are requested from GN.3 and AN.4.

stages.title: Goldfeld’s effective analytic principle
stages.description: Define the degree four completion and the positive inverse Mellin kernel. Prove the positive-measure comparison, the reflection contour identity, the truncated residue formula and the three remainder estimates. From Oesterlé’s exact C1–C4 hypotheses prove a uniform, effectively computed technical class-number bound whose constant depends only on Ψ and M, not on K or G.

stages.title: Two certified rank three curves
stages.description: Construct the native models of E₁₃₉ and E₅₀₇₇ and their source-model comparisons. Import modularity, actual entire elliptic L-functions, quadratic twists, Heegner heights and descent algorithms. Certify conductor 37·139² and 5077, root number −1, arithmetic rank 3, exact vanishing of the first derivative and nonvanishing of the third derivative. Develop the BGZ kernels and rigorous derivative enclosures, including the height gap that upgrades a numerical enclosure to exact zero.

stages.title: Uniform logarithmic class-number bounds
stages.description: Build Ψ,G,M satisfying C1–C4 from the two rank-three newforms. Include every overlap between discriminant and elliptic conductor, all ramified Euler corrections and the finitely many scales M. Certify θ(d)log d≤7000h for every negative fundamental discriminant; certify θ(d)log d≤55h when (d,5077)=1. Prove the fallback split-prime estimate and the exceptional conductor-discriminant case used in class number three.

stages.title: Explicit constants and effective finiteness
stages.description: Define the explicit prime-product majorants C_7000 and C_55 and prove C(t)h≥log d on their stated families. Prove log C_c(t)∼4√(t/log t) by importing PNT from AN.2. Construct a rational algorithm κ(q)>0 and prove the strict lower bound κ(ε)(log d)^(1−ε)<h for every ε>0. Supply an explicit finite cutoff for every prescribed class number, keeping this effective logarithmic bound separate from Siegel’s stronger ineffective power bound.

stages.title: The class number three discriminants
stages.description: Certify the Montgomery–Weinberger exclusion for 10^12≤d≤10^2500 from the three auxiliary real characters, phase inequalities and critical-line-zero brackets. Certify the Lehmer–Lehmer–Shanks small-range sieve above 907, regenerating finite character-pattern certificates. Combine the logarithmic cutoff, the prime-discriminant consequence of genus theory and exact reduced-form enumeration to obtain precisely the sixteen discriminants −23,−31,−59,−83,−107,−139,−211,−283,−307,−331,−379,−499,−547,−643,−883,−907, and largest absolute value 907.
